resolved_items.resolution: The round-trip judge's not-faithful-different classification is sustained. The direct judge incorrectly treated semantic dependencies as though they added separate class-naming and norm-defining conclusions to the audited target proposition.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: Definition 2.5.6 on PDF page 16 (printed page 27) performs two defining acts: it calls random variables satisfying one of Proposition 2.5.2(i)-(iv) sub-gaussian, and it defines the named psi_2 norm by equation (2.13). The proof-free Lean target instead concludes only PsiTwoGauge mu X < top iff there exists a positive real K satisfying SubGaussianSquarePoint mu X K.

resolved_items.item: Whether the target exposes the source's four-property class and naming
resolved_items.resolution: It does not. After unfolding the supplied local dependencies, the target contains only the property-(iv) exponential-square condition and finiteness of its scale infimum. No target conclusion declares a sub-gaussian class, relates membership to all four source properties, or supplies a class predicate whose meaning is that designation. Proposition 2.5.2 in the source explains why property (iv) is extensionally equivalent to (i)-(iii), but inherited source context cannot manufacture a missing Lean conclusion.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: Proposition 2.5.2 on PDF page 13 (printed page 24) lists tail, moment, square-window, and square-point properties (i)-(iv); Definition 2.5.6 on PDF page 16 names their common class. The elaborated target and D001-D004 in direct_review_packet.md mention only PsiTwoGauge, PsiTwoAdmissible, and SubGaussianSquarePoint; the unfolded bodies contain no tail, moment, square-window, or common-class declaration.

resolved_items.item: Whether the target defines the source's infimum norm or merely proves a finiteness theorem
resolved_items.resolution: D001 does implement the numerical infimum formula faithfully, including the exact threshold 2, positive finite scales, and no attainment requirement. But D001 is a semantic dependency used by the selected theorem; its body fixes the referent of PsiTwoGauge and does not change the theorem's top-level conclusion into the source's act of defining the named sub-gaussian norm. The audited declaration itself is therefore a derived finiteness characterization, not the complete two-part definition selected from the source.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: Equation (2.13) on PDF page 16 defines ||X||_{psi_2} as inf {t > 0 : E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2}. D001 defines PsiTwoGauge as sInf of D004-admissible ENNReal scales, while the proof-free target at lines 6-15 of direct_review_packet.md asserts only PsiTwoGauge mu X < top iff existence of a positive SubGaussianSquarePoint witness.

resolved_items.resolution: Neither complete claim implies the other. Lean-to-source fails because the finiteness iff does not deliver the source's class designation or complete named-norm definition. Source-to-Lean fails because Definition 2.5.6 is stated for random variables in the sub-gaussian definition and does not assert the target's universal theorem for every function X, nor specify its ENNReal value and empty-admissible-set behavior outside the source domain. The nonmeasurable branch, where both scale predicates fail, is not genuine strengthening of the selected definition.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: The Lean target universally binds X : Omega -> Real without a binder-level Measurable hypothesis and places Measurable X inside D002 and D004; D001 is ENNReal-valued for every such X. The source calls X a random variable and introduces the norm in the sub-gaussian setting, without an extended-value or empty-set convention.

lean_implies_source.reasoning: Unfolding all relevant dependencies yields a theorem that finiteness of the property-(iv) scale infimum is equivalent to existence of a positive property-(iv) witness. This preserves the core exponential-square formula but does not conclude that the common class of properties (i)-(iv) is called sub-gaussian, and it does not present the selected declaration as the definition of the named psi_2 norm. Consequently the Lean proposition does not imply the full two-part source definition.

source_implies_lean.reasoning: The source names the sub-gaussian class and defines its psi_2 norm by a positive-real infimum. It does not state the exact universal finiteness iff for every function X, or the ENNReal totalization in which nonmeasurable or witness-free functions receive an empty admissible set and gauge top. Those additional order-theoretic and out-of-domain claims are required for the exact Lean proposition, so the selected source result alone does not imply it.

findings.evidence: The source defines the sub-gaussian class and its named psi_2 norm; the Lean target is an iff between finiteness of a gauge and existence of one square-point witness.
findings.impact: The selected target declaration cannot stand as a faithful formal statement of Definition 2.5.6.

findings.evidence: The source explicitly refers to all four equivalent properties (i)-(iv), while the target and its semantic dependencies expose only property (iv) and no common-class predicate or naming conclusion.
findings.impact: The formal target omits one of the source definition's two essential acts.

findings.evidence: The target quantifies over arbitrary functions and totalizes the scale infimum in ENNReal, whereas the source speaks of random variables and defines the norm in the sub-gaussian setting.
findings.impact: The target adds boundary and out-of-domain semantics not asserted by the selected source passage; these do not compensate for the omitted source content.

findings.evidence: D001 and D004 use an infimum over positive finite scales satisfying integrability and the exact bound integral exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2, and D002 expresses the corresponding positive real witness.
findings.impact: The analytic formula underlying property (iv) is accurately represented, but only inside a different top-level finiteness theorem.

rationale: The disagreement turns on the audit boundary. Recursive dependency inspection is required to interpret PsiTwoGauge and SubGaussianSquarePoint, but dependency coverage does not authorize treating every referenced definition as an additional conclusion of the selected theorem. Once D001-D004 are unfolded, the exact target is a square-point finiteness characterization. It accurately contains the equation-(2.13) scale set and avoids an attainment error, yet it neither performs the source's four-property class designation nor states the selected declaration as the definition of the named psi_2 norm. Conversely, the source does not supply the target's universal ENNReal totalization and empty-set behavior. Both implication directions therefore fail, making not-faithful-different the classification and false the accepted flag.
